summary: Defines the Reason header field for SIP. It lets a request or response say why it was sent, such as carrying a cause value from another protocol, for example when a call is cancelled or when a message is created because of an earlier one. It was later updated by RFCs 8606 and 9366.

plainLanguage.summary: The SIP Reason header records why a request was sent. It can carry a SIP status code or a Q.850 cause, so a receiving program can distinguish requests that otherwise look alike.

subtitle: A SIP header that records the protocol and cause behind a request.

tldr.problem: The same SIP request can be sent for different reasons, and a receiver may need to know what caused it to provide the right service or explanation.
tldr.mechanism: The Reason header carries a protocol name, a numeric cause, and optional text. RFC 3326 defines values for SIP status codes and Q.850 causes.
tldr.outcome: The header does not change SIP protocol processing and can be ignored. RFC 3326 is updated by RFC 8606 and RFC 9366.

today: RFC 3326 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists RFC 8606 and RFC 9366 as updates.

sections.title: Why a Request Needs a Cause
sections.content:
A SIP CANCEL request can mean that a call completed on another branch or that the caller stopped waiting. Both stop alerting, but a user interface may want to record them differently.

Third-party call controllers and gateways may also create a SIP request because of another dialog or another protocol. RFC 3326 adds a header that can tell the receiver what triggered a request. It also identifies the Reason header as a possible way to carry a final error code in a provisional response for the Heterogeneous Error Response Forking Problem (HERFP).

The header is initially most useful on BYE and CANCEL. It has no effect on protocol processing, and clients and servers may ignore it.
sections.plainLanguage: A request can look the same even when it was sent for a different reason. The Reason header gives a program extra information to explain or handle that request.

sections.title: The Reason Header Value
sections.content:
A Reason header can contain one or more values. Each value names a protocol and can include semicolon-separated parameters, including a numeric cause and quoted text.

The SIP protocol value means the cause is a SIP status code. Q.850 means the cause is a decimal Q.850 cause value. The syntax also permits other protocol tokens. For example, Reason: SIP ;cause=200 ;text="Call completed elsewhere" records a SIP status code with explanatory text.

The header MAY appear in any request within a dialog, any CANCEL request, and responses whose status code explicitly permits it. A response often needs no Reason header because its status code and reason phrase already explain the result.
sections.plainLanguage: A Reason value says which protocol defines its number and can add a short explanation. The two defined choices are SIP status codes and Q.850 causes.

sections.title: Using and Forwarding Reasons
sections.content:
Any SIP status code MAY appear as a cause in a request. Codes about a user or session parameters can help implement a service; codes about request errors can help with debugging.

A SIP message MAY contain more than one Reason value, but each value MUST name a different protocol. An implementation may ignore a value it does not understand. A proxy that creates a CANCEL after receiving one with a Reason header SHOULD copy the header into its new request.
sections.plainLanguage: A message can carry separate reasons from different protocols. A proxy should preserve the reason when it creates a new CANCEL from an earlier one.

sections.title: Examples of the Cause in Use
sections.content:
When one branch of a forked INVITE succeeds, a proxy can put the successful 200 status in the Reason header of CANCEL requests sent to the other branches. This lets a client distinguish a call completed elsewhere from an abandoned call.

A client that rejects an offer received in a 200 response can include 488 in a Reason header on its BYE. A third-party controller can include 486 when it ends a call because the other user is busy.

For ISUP interworking, a gateway can put Q.850 cause 16 (Normal Call Clearing) from a release message in the Reason header of its SIP CANCEL.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples show how a request can carry the event that caused it: a call answered elsewhere, an unacceptable offer, a busy user, or a release from an ISUP network.

sections.title: Registered Protocol Values
sections.content:
The document defines the SIP Reason header field and an IANA subregistry called Reason Protocols. Each registered protocol value identifies the source and meaning of the cause parameter.

A value must refer to an ITU-T Recommendation, an IETF protocol name, or a recognized protocol identifier from another standards organization. The initial entries are SIP, whose cause is a status code, and Q.850, whose cause is a decimal cause value.
sections.plainLanguage: An official registry lists which protocols can be named in a Reason header. Each entry explains what its cause number means.

sections.title: Protecting the Reason Header
sections.content:
In a HERFP scenario, an attacker who spoofs or removes a Reason header in a response may prevent a client from updating its earlier request correctly. The RFC says this can make session establishment impossible.

For that reason, the Reason header is RECOMMENDED to be protected by a suitable integrity mechanism.
sections.plainLanguage: If someone changes or removes a Reason value, a client may not be able to complete its session. An integrity mechanism can help protect the header from tampering.

viz.caption: REASON HEADER GRAMMAR AND EXAMPLES FROM RFC 3326

data.title: Reason values
data.code:
Reason            =  "Reason" HCOLON reason-value *(COMMA reason-value)
reason-value      =  protocol *(SEMI reason-params)
protocol          =  "SIP" / "Q.850" / token
reason-params     =  protocol-cause / reason-text / reason-extension
protocol-cause    =  "cause" EQUAL cause
cause             =  1*DIGIT
reason-text       =  "text" EQUAL quoted-string

Reason: SIP ;cause=200 ;text="Call completed elsewhere"
Reason: Q.850 ;cause=16 ;text="Terminated"
